title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is the end of §8, 1°, the first worked case of how the strata of the compactified moduli stacks specialise in modular dimension ≤ 2.

What the page does:
(i) Grothendieck says that a full treatment would also describe the universal curve X̂^!_{0,4} → M̂^!_{0,4} ≅ P^1_Z. It has four sections s_0, s_1, s_∞, s_λ (equivalently t_1,…,t_4), and S_4 acts on it by permuting the sections. He declines to do this here.
(ii) He passes to the unordered stack M̂_{0,4} = [M̂^!_{0,4}/S_4].
- The specialisation diagram (76) for the ordered space has 3 arrows. Codim 0 is one vertex carrying the 4 marked points. Codim 1 is the 2+2 graph, i.e. two vertices joined by an edge.
- For the unordered stack this becomes diagram (78): the same picture, but with the arrow carrying multiplicity 1, i.e. a single specialisation.
- Reason: S_4 acts on the λ-line through S_4 → S_3 and permutes the three cusps 0, 1, ∞ transitively. So the stack has a single point at infinity.
(iii) He computes fractional (orbifold) Euler–Poincaré characteristics with compact support.
- χ_!(M^!_{0,4}) = χ_!(P^1 − 3 points) = 2 − 2g − ν = −1.
- χ_!(M̂^!_{0,4}) = χ_!(P^1) = 2.
- For χ_!(M_{0,4}) = χ_!(U_{0,3}, S_4) he stratifies the λ-line by stabilisers.
- Generic points have stabiliser the Klein group V_4, the kernel of S_4 → S_3. It acts trivially on λ but nontrivially on the curve.
- The orbit {−j, −j²} has stabiliser of order 12 (A_4).
- The orbit {1/2, 2, −1} has stabiliser of order 8 (D_4).
- Hence χ = (−6 + 2 + 3)/24 = −1/24. This agrees with the margin shortcut χ_!(U_{0,3})/|S_4| = −1/24, which holds because the quotient is a stack quotient.
(iv) The next page continues the computation.
- χ(M̂_{0,4}) = −1/24 + 3/24 = 1/12.
- It refines this to classes in a Grothendieck ring of stacks: [M_{0,4}] = ¼(T(1) − 1) − 1/24.

Purpose: to calibrate the stratification of M̂_{g,ν} at infinity by MD-graphs against simple invariants, as orbifold 'multiplicities', before treating M_{1,1} and the other cases of dimension ≤ 2.
errors: The written line '= −1 + 1/3 + 1/2 = −1/24' is arithmetically −1/6 as written. The terms −1, 1/3, 1/2 are the S_3-quotient contributions (−6/6, 2/6, 3/6). The extra factor 1/4 from the generic V_4 stabiliser, which gives −1/24, is silently omitted. The final value −1/24 is correct, and the margin NB gets it directly.
Minor: the transcription's 𝕄^{an}_{0,3} should be the λ-line U^{an}_{0,3} (the image shows a script/blackboard U or B).

ideas.what: Universal curve over M̂^!_{0,4} ≅ P^1 with four sections and S_4 action (mentioned, not carried out)
ideas.modern_name: universal stable curve over M̄_{0,4} / Legendre family, S_4 symmetry

ideas.what: Unordered moduli as stack quotient [M^!_{0,4}/S_4]; the Klein four-group acts trivially on the λ-line, and the three cusps merge into one boundary point with multiplicity-1 specialisation
ideas.modern_name: stack quotient, generic stabiliser V_4 of M_{0,4}/S_4
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{0,4} and S_4 at a general level

ideas.what: Fractional Euler characteristics χ_! of DM stacks computed by stratifying by stabiliser type; χ(M_{0,4}) = −1/24, χ(M̂_{0,4}) = 1/12

deep.surprise_reason: Standard orbifold Euler characteristic bookkeeping for M_{0,4} and its S_4 quotient, with a small slip in an intermediate line. The more interesting Grothendieck-ring (motivic class of stacks) refinement is on the next page, not here.
transcription_corrections: 'Caractéristiques d'EP fonctionnaires' should read 'Caractéristiques d'EP fractionnaires' (fractional Euler–Poincaré characteristics).
'par un diagramme presque analogue' is likely 'par un diagramme purement numérique' or similar (uncertain).
In the S_4-quotient line, '𝕄^{an}_{0,3}' should be 'U^{an}_{0,3}' (the λ-line).
The crossed-out symbol over M^{an}_{0,4} on the third χ line is a struck-through decoration (hat/!), so the intended object is the unordered M_{0,4}.
Diagram (78): codim 0 is a single vertex labelled 4; the arrow carries multiplicity 1; codim 1 is two vertices each labelled 2 joined by an edge.
